publish-boundary-test.ref: server/killSwitchSharing.test.ts (13) + server/publishChokePoint.test.ts (13). socialPublish.ts changed in two ways and both are covered. (1) The kill-switch check was EXTRACTED to killSwitchBlockedPlatforms so igAutopost — an autonomous cron measured at 116 live posts in prod — could share the operator's emergency stop instead of bypassing it. killSwitchSharing.test.ts pins the guard's decisions (global / publishing / per-platform, the DENY audit record naming WHICH switch fired, and the deliberate fail-open when switch state is unreadable) AND pins that the extraction left publishToSocial behaviourally identical — including the partial-block case where one platform is stopped and the other still publishes, which is the behaviour most likely to be lost in an extraction. (2) A `link` field was added, because its absence was WHY nickActions.socialPost reached around the door to metaSocial.socialPost; pinned through to postToFacebook. publishChokePoint.test.ts holds the claim gates at contentAdmin.publishCarousel and nickActions.socialPost, and adds a structural sweep asserting no NEW file can import the low-level publishers — the part that makes it stick, since adStudio was fixed alone on 2026-07-25 and this identical defect survived on three other surfaces. Both structural assertions red-green verified: planting a file that imports postToInstagram fails the sweep by name; removing igAutopost's guard branch while keeping the call fails its pin. CADENCE IS NOT CLAIMED — this change deliberately did NOT apply the feed cap to igAutopost, because policy v7 sets maxFeedPostsPerDay=2 while the autoposter has been doing 3/day on 8 of the last 14 active days, and that conflict is the operator's to resolve, not this PR's to decide silently. PR #1127.

cron-fail-closed.ref: server/ros083ReviewQueue.test.ts (6), mutation-verified three ways. The cron file changed here is cron/jobs/reviewRequests.ts, and the change is a DIRECTION change on failure, so the fail-closed question is the right one to ask of it. BEFORE: the handler caught everything and returned { recordsProcessed: 0 }. Both runners record a RESOLVED handler as `completed` (cron/index.ts:218, cron/scheduler.ts:418) and log `failed` only when the handler THROWS — so an outage on the job that texts customers was filed in cron_log as a successful run that did nothing. AFTER: it re-throws. WHY THAT IS STILL FAIL-CLOSED, checked rather than assumed: (1) the throw happens BEFORE the send loop and before any row is claimed — getPendingReviewRequests is read up front, and claimReviewRequest (the atomic pending->sent claim) is only reached inside the loop, so no partial send and no half-claimed row is possible on this path; (2) neither runner retries a failed handler — grep for retry/attempt in cron/scheduler.ts and cron/index.ts finds no retry loop on the job path, so the job simply waits for its next 30-minute interval and a throw cannot re-fire it within the tick; (3) lock behaviour is UNCHANGED, which is the property that actually protects against duplicate SMS: scheduler.ts releases the lock in `finally` for both the resolved and the thrown path and withholds it only on TIMEOUT (timedOut stays false for a thrown error), so this change does not touch the zombie-handler protection at all; (4) the daily cap and quiet-hours gates are untouched. WHAT THE THROW BUYS: cron/observer.ts counts CONSECUTIVE `failed` rows per job and raises the job once it crosses its threshold, reading error_message. Under the old swallow this job could never produce a `failed` row, so it was structurally invisible to the failure observer no matter how long it had been broken. Also fixed in the same file: `recordsProcessed: typeof result === "number" ? result : 0` was never true — processReviewRequestQueue returns an object from all five of its exits and always has — so every run this job has ever made logged recordsProcessed: 0, including runs that sent real SMS; it now reports result.processed with a `details` string carrying the decline reason, so a legitimate zero (cap reached, quiet hours, gateway offline) is legible as a decision rather than as nothing happening. Mutations verified RED and each file restored byte-identical: re-swallowing in the catch turns 1 case red, restoring the typeof branch turns 1 case red, restoring the [] on getReviewRequests turns 1 case red. NOT CLAIMED: no live cron run and no prod cron_log observation — the assertions above about runner behaviour are read from cron/index.ts and cron/scheduler.ts, not measured against a deployed tick.

operator-walkthrough.ref: WHAT THE OPERATOR SEES, on a phone — /admin -> Today, the "Integration freshness" card (ALG / ShopDriver).  THE ARITHMETIC IS THE BUG, so it is worth stating exactly. The card is classified from the AGE OF THE LAST SUCCESS against staleAfterMinutes = 24h (OverviewSection.tsx:260), and the server read selected only rows with `outcome = 'success'`. Put those together: ALG authentication starts failing at 9:00am; at 9:12 the card reads emerald "Fresh · 12m old"; at 2pm it reads emerald "Fresh · 300m old"; it does not turn amber until 9:00am THE NEXT DAY. Through all of it, every probe is writing an `auth_failed` row that this query never selected. A full business day of a dead integration, rendered green.  AFTER: the same outage renders red — "ALG / ShopDriver · Auth failing · 6 failed probes since the last success · last success 03/08/2026, 08:55". The last-success timestamp is deliberately KEPT on a failing card, because it is the most useful number there (it says how long the outage has been running); what changed is that it is no longer the only thing shown.  A SECOND STATE, on the same card: when our own probe log cannot be read, the query used to return `connected: false`, which the classifier rendered as "Offline" — a confident claim about ALG made entirely on evidence about OUR database. It now reports `readable: false` and renders amber "Unknown — the probe log could not be read". The client also passes react-query's own isError into `readable`, because a query that never resolved cannot report anything about itself.  WHAT WAS DELIBERATELY NOT DONE, and this is the interesting half: the tempting fix is to count every row in alg_probe_log as evidence of life. That would be a WORSE false-green than the one being fixed. `dedup` means the probe budget guard SKIPPED the probe — it never reached ALG at all — so a permanently dead integration that keeps getting skipped would look busy and healthy, and would survive even a total outage. AUTH_ATTEMPTING_OUTCOMES in lib/adminActivity.ts already draws exactly that line for the session-resume throttle, so it is REUSED rather than re-listed, and `lastSuccessfulAt` still anchors on `outcome = 'success'` alone. Both of those are pinned by tests so the next reader cannot "simplify" them back.  The failure count is a STREAK, not a history — the server stops counting at the first non-failing attempt, so one bad probe last Tuesday does not keep the card red today, and the scan is bounded at ATTEMPT_WINDOW = 20 because this query refetches every 60 seconds.  EVIDENCE: client/src/__tests__/ros083AlgFreshness.test.ts (7) + server/ros083AlgProbeSelection.test.ts (5), MUTATION-VERIFIED THREE WAYS — ignoring the failure streak turns 2 cases red, letting the unreadable branch fall through turns 2 red, widening the attempt set to include `dedup` turns 1 red; every file restored byte-identical (0 residual markers). The four pre-existing classifier contracts (fresh / stale / offline / unknown on the old inputs) are re-asserted in the new file so the added states cannot silently move them, and a call with no failure fields at all still returns `fresh`. Full serial suite green: 389 files passed / 2 skipped, 4,820 passed / 50 skipped / 1 todo, exit 0. tsc --noEmit clean.  NOT CLAIMED: no live production observation and no prod alg_probe_log read — the outage above is described from the code path, not measured against a deployed failure. NOTE ON THIS KEY: last-writer-wins by design; the manifest lives on main while requirements are derived per-diff, so this text describes the most recently merged operator-facing change and nothing else.

capability-ledger-updated.deferred: No capability gains or loses a state, so no ledger entry is edited. The rule fires on one changed router file: server/routers/adminSecurity.ts, and specifically on its `integrationFreshness` query. Nothing nickstire CAN DO changed. No surface is exposed, no procedure is added or removed, no auth boundary moves (it was and remains adminProcedure), no provider, cost, publish, send or generation path is touched, and the healthy path is behaviourally identical — a green integration still renders `Fresh · Nm old` from the same `lastSuccessfulAt`, computed from the same `outcome = 'success'` query, which this change deliberately did not widen. What changed is what the card SAYS when the integration is broken: it gained two additional read-only fields (the most recent auth-attempting probe and the consecutive-failure streak) and a `failing` state, plus a `readable` flag that separates 'our probe log is unreadable' from 'ALG is offline'. That is a truthfulness fix to an existing operator signal, not a new capability, and the ledger tracks capabilities. The nearest entry is `operator-command-center` (integration_verified, operator_only) and it is NOT the right home: it describes the reel policy / spend / approvals / lineage console, whose evidence is server/commandCenter.test.ts, and it has no relationship to the ALG probe log or to the Today overview card this change touches. Attaching this work there would make that entry describe something it does not cover, which is worse than leaving it alone. There is no ledger entry for the ALG / ShopDriver integration itself, and this PR deliberately does not create one: registering a capability is a claim about what the system does, and the honest state for ALG here would have to be asserted from a live probe run against production, which this change has not done and does not claim. EVIDENCE for the behaviour change lives on the operator-walkthrough entry: client/src/__tests__/ros083AlgFreshness.test.ts (7) + server/ros083AlgProbeSelection.test.ts (5), mutation-verified three ways, with the four pre-existing classifier contracts re-asserted so the added states cannot silently move them.
